item: RQO 05-24: whether Commissioner Gimenez has a voting conflict on matters where his son's employer appears before the BCC (Commission held he may participate and vote)
party: Bilzin, Sumberg, Baena, Price and Axelrod (appears before the BCC on land use and zoning matters)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics and Public Trust, Advisory Opinion RQO 05-24 (Mar 3, 2005)

quote: your son is an associate with the firm Bilzin, Sumberg, Baena, Price and Axelrod. Bilzin Sumberg regularly appears before the Board of County Commissioners on land use and zoning matters.

item: INQ 11-133: whether private companies employing the Mayor's sons may transact business with the County (yes; sons hold no controlling interest)
party: Private companies that employ the Mayor's sons (not named in the summary)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2011, INQ 11-133

quote: Private companies that employ sons of the mayor may transact business with the Co. because the sons have no controlling financial interests (≥ 10%) in the companies.

item: INQ 12-96: recommendation that the Mayor assign supervision of bids involving MCM to his deputies
party: MCM (construction company bidding on County work)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-96

quote: It was recommended that the Mayor assign authority to supervise bids involving MCM construction company to his deputies because MCM employs one of his sons.

item: INQ 12-150: Mayor no longer constrained on future MCM contracts once his son left MCM; precautions apply if the son's new employer seeks County contracts

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-150

quote: The Mayor is no longer constrained from negotiating future contracts with MCM because Julio Gimenez, a son of the Mayor, no longer works for MCM.

item: INQ 12-150: if the son's new employer seeks County contracts, the Mayor should follow the INQ 11-133 precautions

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-150

quote: if the company now employing his son, Facchina, were to seek contracts from the County, the Mayor should follow the precautions previously provided to him in INQ 11-133.

item: INQ 12-158: Mayor had delegated oversight of a County contract while his son's employer held it; may now participate because the successor company does not employ his son
party: Company that employed the Mayor's son, holder of a County contract (not named in the summary)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-158

quote: Although the Mayor properly delegated authority to another while a company that employed his son was engaged in a County contract, the Mayor may now participate in oversight of the contract

item: INQ 13-03: Mayor may now support resolutions on 3 County contracts MCM bid on; he had delegated MCM procurement oversight while his son worked there

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2013, INQ 13-03

quote: Since the Mayor’s son is no longer employed by MCM, a company that had bid on 3 County contracts, the Mayor may now support resolutions impacting those contracts.

item: INQ 12-63: School Board may contract with the County for head-start grants and the Mayor may act on School Board matters despite his wife's School Board employment

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-63

quote: Employment by the Mayor’s wife with the School Board does not prohibit the School Board from contracting with the County for head-start grants & does not prevent the Mayor from participating in actions affecting the School Board

item: INQ 12-180: Mayor should delegate monitoring of a County contract held by his daughter-in-law's employer
party: Daughter-in-law's employer, County contractor (not named in the summary)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-180

quote: Although the mayor’s daughter-in-law is not involved in a contract between her employer and the County, the mayor should delegate a staff member to monitor the contract

item: INQ 12-219: Mayor may carry out functions related to bond counsel where his daughter-in-law is employed

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2012, INQ 12-219

quote: Nothing in the County Ethics Code precludes the Mayor from carrying out functions related to bond counsel Squires Sanders, where the Mayor’s daughter-in- law is employed but is not a partner

item: INQ 19-43 (requested by Julio F. Gimenez, Principal, Miami-Dade Steel, LLC): the Mayor's son's company may contract with the County if the Mayor does not participate; the Mayor formally recused himself under Charter s. 5.03(D)

record.label: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics, Summary of Informal Opinions 2019, INQ 19-43

quote: The son of the County Mayor may transact business and enter into a contract with the County through his privately-owned company, provided that the Mayor shall not participate in the transaction in any manner

quote: his son, Carlos J. “CJ” Gimenez, who represented Formula One parties in negotiations to bring racing to the City of Miami in 2018, no longer represents any interests involved in the current initiative.
